cards.text: Right before this comes a call: "Come, let us return to the LORD." It says He'll come to them like the spring showers that water the earth. Now God speaks to Ephraim, the northern kingdom of Israel, and to Judah, the southern kingdom: "What shall I do with you, O Ephraim? What shall I do with you, O Judah?"

cards.question: God says their loyalty is like a morning mist, like the early dew. His point is that their loyalty lasts and lasts.

cards.text: Their loyalty is like a morning mist: here at sunrise, GONE before you find your car keys. So God says He has hewn them and slain them by the words of His mouth.

cards.question: God has hewn them by the ___, slaying them with the words of His mouth.

cards.text: And His judgments go forth like lightning. Then God says what He desires instead of sacrifice.

cards.question: God says He desires something, not sacrifice. What is it?
God says He wants burnt offerings more than the knowledge of God.

cards.text: Friend, that's like handing someone the fanciest cookie box in town and never ONCE asking how they're doing. But God says they have transgressed the covenant, like someone from way back at the very beginning.

cards.question: God says they've transgressed the covenant like someone from the very beginning. Who is it?

cards.text: There, they were unfaithful to Him. Then God gets specific: Gilead is a city of evildoers, tracked with footprints of blood.

cards.question: On the way to Shechem, a band of ___ lies in ambush like raiders.

cards.text: PRIESTS. Murdering on the road like raiders, committing atrocities. That's finding out the lifeguard is the one pushing people INTO the pool.
Then God says that in the house of Israel, He has seen a horrible thing.

cards.question: What is the horrible thing God has seen in the house of Israel?

cards.text: Israel is defiled. Then God turns to Judah and says a harvest is appointed for them too.

cards.question: God tells Judah a harvest is appointed. When does He say it will be?

answers.text: When He restores His people from captivity
When Judah rebuilds the city walls
When Judah crowns a brand new king

cards.text: God keeps going. Now He talks about the day He heals Israel.

cards.question: When God heals Israel, the iniquity of Ephraim will be ___.

cards.text: Like a doctor peeling back the bandage, and the whole room goes OOOH: the crimes of Samaria, capital of the northern kingdom, are exposed too. For they practice deceit, thieves break in, and bandits raid in the streets.

cards.question: After all those crimes, God says the people take it to heart that He remembers all their evil.

cards.text: Nope, they don't give it a thought, but their deeds are all around them, right before His face. That's me wondering where the batch went with crumbs ALL over my apron.

cards.question: They delight the king with their evil. How do they delight the princes?

cards.text: Then God pulls out a picture, and friend, this is MY department. They're all adulterers, like an oven heated by a baker.

cards.question: In God's oven picture, the baker has to keep stoking the fire from the kneading to the rising of the dough.

cards.text: Most ovens you gotta babysit, but this one runs hot ALL by itself, and believe me, that is NOT a compliment. On the day of our king, the princes are inflamed with wine.

cards.question: The princes are inflamed with wine on the day of our king. Who does the king join hands with?

cards.text: They prepare their heart like an oven while they lie in wait. All night their anger smolders.

cards.question: Their anger smolders all night, and by morning it cools off.

cards.text: In the morning, their anger blazes like a flaming fire. Their loyalty was like a morning mist, but THIS? Shows up in the morning right on time.

cards.question: God says all of them are hot as an oven. What do they devour?
All their kings fall, and not one of them calls upon God.

findings.problem: The opening card retells and quotes Hosea 6:1-3, which belongs to the passage before this one, and cites Hosea 6:1-4. That range falls outside both the passage (Hosea 6:4-7:7) and the stop (Hosea 6:4-11). The card should give context in its own words and cite only Hosea 6:4.

rule.text: The passage right before it is also provided, for context only. It is not part of the lesson.

findings.problem: The card says Ephraim is the northern kingdom of Israel and Judah is the southern kingdom. Hosea 6:4 doesn't say this, and the card gives no reference for these outside facts.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: The card calls Samaria the capital of the northern kingdom. Hosea 7:1 doesn't say this, and the card gives no reference for this outside fact.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: The only setup is that God will heal Israel. Healing points a thoughtful baker toward 'forgotten', not 'exposed'. The blank also asks the baker to finish the wording of the line, when it should test meaning they can reason out. Give more context on the story card, or ask about the meaning instead.

rule.text: The check: could a thoughtful baker who has only seen the earlier cards make a reasoned pick? If the only way to get it right is luck, give the story card more context or ask a different question.

findings.problem: The card asks the baker to complete the second half of a poetic parallel ('and the princes with ___'). That is guessing the next words of a line in a prophetic passage, like the Psalm 23 'anoint David's head with' bad example.

rule.text: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.

findings.problem: From card 4 to the end, the question types alternate in a strict pattern: true or false, multiple choice, true or false, multiple choice, true or false, multiple choice, true or false. True or false also leads the stop 4 to 1 over fill in the blank.

rule.text: No formula. Which question type comes next, the order the types come in and where a blank falls are chosen naturally for each card. They never follow a pattern. No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: The card tells Hosea 7:6 and makes a callback to Hosea 6:4 (the morning mist). Under the 'first verse to last' rule, that gives the range Hosea 6:4-7:6, which is wider than what the card actually tells and runs across both stops.
findings.question: When a story card uses two far-apart verses, for example a callback to an earlier verse, should it cite the full range between them, only the verses it uses (like Hosea 6:4, 7:6), or only the new verse it tells?
